text:
GONG 
Your call is ready 
Encord & Covera Health | Trial Support Session 
Covera Health • Mar 25, 2026 • 33 minutes 
Encord: Kamil Mouthon • Customer: Craig Irvine + 3 more 
Go to call 
Generate follow-up email 
Key points 1. Slice Counting: Encord's slice counting is 0-indexed, while the PACS system is 1-indexed, causing potential errors when manually transferring notes. Skander confirmed this can be amended. 
2. PACS Integration: Covera Health cannot push data directly to PACS systems due to the level of integration required, which is a fundamental limitation of their current workflow. 
3. Dynamic Tile Layout: The current system has issues with dynamically adding tiles, causing the series selector to disappear and the layout to become stuck. Users cannot change the tile layout on the fly within a task, but it can be set at a project or task level. 
4. Reference Lines: The ability to see reference lines (crosshairs) moving across multiple tiles is crucial for MR workflows, particularly for identifying vertebrae in axial views. 
5. Left/Right Indicators: The absence of left/right, anterior/posterior indicators is a concern, especially for spine imaging, where it's critical for accurate diagnosis and surgery. This is a standard feature in PACS systems. 
6. Measurement Tool Functionality: The measurement tool has several issues: the arrow head doesn't align with the measurement, numbers are hard to select and cannot be moved, and visibility is poor, hindering comparison of sizes. 
7. Window Level Adjustment: Jacob reported that the window level adjustment via dragging is not dynamically updating effectively for some radiographs, requiring excessive dragging to change image contrast, which significantly impacts review efficiency. 
8. Global Classification: The VCF addendum flag, currently at the series level, needs to be a global classification applied at the study level to prevent it from disappearing when switching views. 
9. Addendum Logic: There is a need for logic

6. POC Proposal: Matt proposes a two-week Proof of Concept (POC) to provide 100-150 hours of premium, annotated egocentric data for Noble Machine to evaluate its impact on model performance. 
7. Customizable Annotation: Vineeth highlights Encord's ability to customize annotation ontologies based on Noble Machine's specific needs and existing training patterns, ensuring the enrichment is precisely what they require.

text:
Hi Hugo,

thanks for reaching out and for your questions!

I came across Encord because I am looking for an annotation tool for a 
GenAI Template Filling model.
It's Named Entity Recognition with the twist of connecting entities 
together to build a "record" of a product described by a document.

Virtually all tools I have looked at so far, support the standard NLP 
tasks (classification, NER, etc.) which do not natively fit my need.

The team consists of 10 people and we would like to launch the first 
annotation tasks in around 2 weeks.
We already have the data to be labelled and the model predictions.
We just need a tool to allow annotators to fill in a form based on a 
document.

Let me know if this is something that can be tackled by Encord and what 
the annual costs would be.

Best,

Lucas

subject: RE: Encord - commercial proposal + catch-up on Monday
text:
Encord Team,

Thank you for sharing the Order Form. We're close on the overall scope and are excited about the potential partnership. Before moving forward, we'd like to propose a set of revisions to better align with our operational requirements and standard procurement practices.

Below are some key proposed changes:

1. Payment Structure & Financial Risk
Current: 100% annual fee invoiced upfront
Proposed Revision:

  *   Move to quarterly billing or milestone-based payments tied to delivery and/or meeting performance benchmarks
  *   Introduce a 10-20% holdback tied to compliance and acceptance criteria
  *   Include a refund or credit mechanism for undelivered or non-conforming services
2. Service Levels & Performance Metrics
Current: "Commercially reasonable efforts" with benchmarks defined post-contract
Proposed Revision:

  *   Define SLAs upfront, including:
     *   Turnaround time: Target 5 business days per batch (~75 sequences/week)
     *   Throughput: Minimum weekly delivery capacity aligned to ~75 sequences/week
     *   Quality: accuracy thresholds (to be aligned based on training period results)
  *   Replace "commercially reasonable efforts" with measurable, enforceable SLAs
  *   Include service credits or remedies for missed SLAs
3. Benchmarking & Acceptance Criteria
Current: Benchmarks defined after project start
Proposed Revision:

  *   Establish benchmark quality and processing metrics prior to contract execution (these can be defined during the initial training period prior to commencement of the annual contract)
  *   Attach these benchmarks as a contract exhibit
  *   Ensure benchmarks cannot be unilaterally adjusted
4. Acceptance & Rework Terms
Current: 72-hour acceptance window; work deemed accepted thereafter
Proposed Revision:

  *   Extend acceptance window to 5 business days (recognizing internal QA workflows and time zone differences)
  *   Add a latent defect provision (e.g., 30 days) for quality issues not immediately detectable
